brief: A three-storey cabinet with at least three drawers.

requirements.evidence: Two columns of full hex bases at (0,0) and (1,0) across levels 0, 1 and 2 (six bases), so the build is three storeys tall. Open faces are capped and joints locked; check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
Three notch drawer frames (hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm) at (0,1) on levels 0, 1 and 2, each set between the two adjacent columns, one per storey.

finish.summary: Built a three-storey cabinet: a 2x3 block of full hex bases (columns at (0,0) and (1,0), levels 0-2) with three drawer frames set into the open position at (0,1), one per storey. Open faces were capped and joints locked; the configurator check is clear. Caveats: the drawers are the frames only, and I did not add drawer fronts or contents. The build has 65 parts and a large print estimate (about 3.7 kg and 93 hours by the budget), above the roughly 40-part guideline, because three storeys of two columns were needed. Material, strength and load ratings are not checked by the configurator.

M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
